## NEW FINDING 2026-08-24 — COVERAGE GAP, not platform movement
## AGENT IDENTITY (SPIFFE) — a NEW IAM PRINCIPAL TYPE   [reported 2026-08-24, HIGH/AISPM]
Found by following the "admins can view an agent's SPIFFE ID on the Agent details page
(Public Preview)" line into the IAM + Agent Platform governance docs. Both render fully:
  docs.cloud.google.com/iam/docs/agent-identity-overview
  docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/govern/agent-identity-overview

ID format:      spiffe://TRUST_DOMAIN/resources/SERVICE/RESOURCE_PATH
IAM policy:     **principal://**TRUST_DOMAIN/resources/SERVICE/RESOURCE_PATH
  e.g. principal://agents.global.org-123456789012.system.id.goog/resources/aiplatform/
       projects/9876543210/locations/us-central1/reasoningEngines/my-test-agent

*** ACTION ITEM #1: any IAM parser that knows serviceAccount: / user: / group: / domain:
    but NOT principal:// will read an agent-bound policy as having NO agent bindings. ***

Credentials: X.509 auto-provisioned at deploy, **RENEWED EVERY 24 HOURS**.
vs service accounts (Google's own framing): agent identities "are not shared by multiple workloads
  by default, CAN'T BE IMPERSONATED, and don't allow developers to generate long-lived service
  account keys."  => INVERTS the posture question: not "who can mint SA keys" but
  **"WHICH AGENTS STILL RUN ON A SERVICE ACCOUNT INSTEAD OF AN AGENT IDENTITY."**
Authenticates to: MCP SERVERS, cloud resources, OTHER AGENTS, external tools/services.
TWO PRIVILEGE ENVELOPES on one principal:
  own authority   — bound access tokens (GCP); 2-legged OAuth / API keys / HTTP basic (external)
  on behalf of user — 3-LEGGED OAUTH, bounded by the user's consent
  Audit logs DISTINGUISH the two ("acting as itself" vs "on behalf of an end user").
  *** AIDR signal: agent acting under OWN authority on data it only ever reached ON BEHALF OF
      a user = privilege escalation, visible in these logs and NOWHERE ELSE. ***
Governance surfaces to inventory: IAM allow AND DENY policies; **Principal Access Boundary (PAB)**;
  VPC Service Controls; DEFAULT Context-Aware Access policies enforcing **mTLS + DPoP token
  binding** (a relaxed CAA policy is a detectable downgrade from the documented default).
Console caveat: if the publisher does not publish a SPIFFE ID, the Agent details page falls back to
  the **Agent Registry resource ID** => console is NOT a uniform source of agent identity, and a
  fallback ID is itself the signal that an agent runs WITHOUT an attested identity.

## MIS-MAPPING HAZARD THAT CAUSED THE MISS
2026-08-10 reported "Agent Identity" — that was MICROSOFT'S **Entra Agent ID**. Different thing.
Model "attested per-agent identity" ONCE with per-vendor bindings: Entra Agent ID / Google SPIFFE
agent identity / AgentCore workload access tokens. Do not treat as three unrelated features.

first-class record type + IAM governance policies in private preview. Custom MCP server data stores
GA (Aug 7, off by default behind an org-policy constraint). Automatic tools/list discovery (Aug 6).

Agent Studio SSRF fix — discloses that Agent Studio AUTO-GENERATES an /api-proxy backend endpoint.
